full_text:
I’ll start off telling you a bit about what we’re doing – are you on the Network 75?

Yeah.

We have mainly been interviewing female students that are going on the sandwich year placement and we’ve done that, because we want to interview women about their first experiences of the engineering industry. We want to find out what their expectations and things like that are, but we’ve had a few problems at [university], finding female students that are actually going on placement so we’ve broadened the scope a bit and decided to include the Network 75 students because they’ve obviously got experience of the engineering industry as well. So I’ll start off asking you a bit about why you decided to do engineering and that sort of thing and then ask you a bit about the placement really. What course is it that you’re doing?

I’m doing electrical – electronic and it’s a degree.

OK, did you do your ‘A’ levels?

Er, I done a National Diploma (right) electronics before I come here.

Yeah, Ok, did you do that at a different college or..?

I did it at [name] College and that was for 2 years.

Yeah, OK. What type of school did you go to before that?

Erm, just ordinary – it was a comprehensive school I went to.

Yeah, it wasn’t a girls’ school or anything like that?

No, nothing like that.

OK, just before you started on the – started at [university], have you had any previous work experience?

Erm, well when I first left school I’d done – I started off doing a computer course at college but I didn’t like that (yeah) so I finished there and then I worked, for the rest of the year, up until the September and I worked in erm [company], and then I went back to college and I done ‘A’ levels and I didn’t like them so I quit and then I went and worked in [company] out in [place] and then that’s when I decided to do electronics at college then.

Yeah, OK. What do you think it is that made you decide to do electronics then?

Erm, I wanted to do something a bit different ‘cos I’d already done ‘A’ levels – I didn’t like doing them, and I’d done the computer course – I just found everything a bit boring, I wanted something different. And working in [company], I know it’s only on the production line, but I was interested and I actually applied for an apprenticeship with [company] and I went for the interview and I never got the job and I felt that was because I was a girl (really?) – yeah – and, and then I thought I’ll go out and do it myself and then I went to college.

Excellent – OK. Did you know any other engineers to talk to or anything like that?

Mm, I didn’t know anyone when I went back to college, ‘cos I was two years older than the rest of ‘em then as well, so it was scary (yeah). But when I first started the course in college, there were 2 other girls there so I was pleased with that. But then, they both dropped out within their first year (really?) – yeah, so I was left on my own then.

With like how many …?

I was the only girl. I mean there must have been about 20 plus. (Really?) Yeah.

Are you the only girl on your course now?

Yeah.

Did it ever bother you that it was so male dominated at all or…?

Erm, I – mm, well when I first started – even in college as well, you find they won’t speak to you – the boys – they, they go off in their own little gang, but then give it a couple of months and they come round and it just – it don’t feel no different now. (Yeah) Erm, just – they say oh, you’re one of the lads but I don’t - I don’t really see why it should be a male orient – orientated subject really. I don’t see why it should be a man’s subject and not a woman’s.

OK, do you think that more women should be encouraged to do engineering then?

Erm, I don’t know about encouraged but make it a bit easier – make it not seem so erm you can’t do it because you’re a woman (yeah). If they want to do it, they should – it should be made easier.

Yeah, to get into. OK, what do you think makes a good engineer?

Mm, I dunno. These are hard questions, isn’t it? Erm, (pause) erm, I can’t – I dunno.

That’s OK. Do you think that there are any particular advantages or disadvantages to being a woman in engineering, or a woman in a male dominated environment?

Erm, a lot of – well, being at Uni, they all reckon that I’m just gonna pass just ‘cos I’m a girl (right). Erm, but I wouldn’t say there’s many advantages in work – maybe, maybe people think that I’d get a job more easier because I’m a woman (yeah) but it don’t feel that way in work, it just feels equal, it don’t feel that I’m given anything to do because I’m a woman (yeah) and like when I say I don’t want to do something I still gotta do it. If I say I don’t want to get my hands dirty, they say you’ve still gotta do it, yeah.

OK, has the course been what you expected it to be?

Erm, in college it was – yeah, and then coming to Uni is a bit of a – a jump up. I found it a bit harder than I thought it was going to be here. Erm, but a lot of the stuff was what I thought it was going to be. It’s – I’d say it was a lot harder but I’m learning the stuff I wanted to learn.

When you went to college, did you know that you wanted to come to Uni afterwards, or did you decide that when you got to the end of it?

Mm, no I thought I could leave college and just go into work, but then during college I thought ah, I want to get an even better job so I come to Uni then.

Ok then, what have been the best and the worst things about the course so far?

Erm, oh, well the worst thing so far has been the exams at the end of the year. Erm, and having to get to know everyone else when we’ve come up here, ‘cos I think it was only last 2 weeks that I actually spoke to the rest of ‘em., during exam time, I’d never spoke to ‘em all the way through the year, really. (Yeah) Erm, erm, the best bits – I dunno – I can’t say oh I love it here, I love learning and – but I just enjoy – what it is I can’t say I love coming to Uni and doing all that work but I found the exams at the end of year the hardest because in college you erm – do little exams, everytime we’ve done a subject you sort of do little modules, whereas here you have to learn it all and do exams at the end.

Do you have to do mostly exams and not coursework?

Erm, they’re coursework as well, I think they’re like split 70/30 and 50/50 but they were 3 hour exams – I don’t think I’ve ever sat an exam that long before.

I hate exams (laughs)

So it just – it just finished last week, now. So I’m working full time at the moment.

Do you usually do that through all the holidays, do you work full time for the company?

Yeah.

OK, have you been taught by any female lecturers at all?

Erm, there was one in college. Erm, first of all she started off just being a Maths teacher and then she taught some electronic subjects as well, but have I got any up here? No, I haven’t been taught by any up here – no.

Really? Would you find it encouraging, do you think, to have more female lecturers?

Erm, I don’t really think you would.

As long as the teachers are good…

Yeah.

That’s OK. Do you think that the lecturers treat you the same as the male students?

Mm, I don’t think they do to start with, I feel – I don’t say they treat me different it’s just little – little ways they speak to me or they talk to the whole class, boys, oh and girl, that sort of thing but come the first couple of weeks say, after that I’m just treated the same then. I think it’s just initially, at the beginning. It’s the same in work, when you meet different engineers they all won’t swear round me, and they all act differently, but that only lasts for the first couple of weeks and then they’re all the same then.

Yeah. Just like the shock of seeing a woman? OK, do you have to do much group work as part of this Uni course?

Erm, what you mean as part of the course year?

Yeah.

Erm, what happens is on a Wednesday, I think the people who come here work in groups to do little projects, but I miss out that lesson because I do that sort of thing in work. (yeah) And, instead of completing the lesson, I have to fill in a log book (right) of the stuff I do at work. So I – mm, if we do any practicals we get in groups of 2 or 3 (yeah) that’d only be for the one lesson.

OK, do you use the skills that you’ve learnt at Uni in work, do you think?

Erm, I’m just starting to now. When I first went there, erm not really – nothing I learnt in college – I couldn’t say really I used in work, but now I’m starting to pick up things and erm when we go on site, I seem to understand it a bit more now. I wouldn’t say I use anything I know, at the moment, but I seem to understand things more because of what I’ve learnt here.

Yeah. Do you think it works the other way round as well? Do you think what you learn at work helps you understand things better at University?

Yeah, definitely the other way round (yeah). It’s like erm, when you’re sat in the class and you learn all this and I thought do I really – have I really got to know all this? (yeah) Erm, and then when you go out to work then, you see why you have to know it. Maybe you don’t have to know it word for word in your head, because you’ll be able to look at books and instructions, but you see what it’s all used for then, when you go out to work.

Yeah, OK. Why did you want to do the Network 75 programme? What appealed to you about doing that?

Hmm, the money (yeah). Erm, I did apply for the sandwich year anyway, I wanted to do a year out, but I’d just moved out of – out from my mum’s and I’d bought my own place, and I really wanted to come here and I couldn’t afford to support myself and pay the fees (yeah) and I saw that – I heard about the Network 75 and erm, at first when they come to college I was like no, no, I ain’t going to that, there’s got to be some catch (yeah) and someone gave me the phone number, I just rung up and then they found me a place and I was like oh, great. And I’m glad I done it now.

Yeah, OK. Do you think that you would have come to Uni then if you hadn’t had the Network 75 thing?

Erm, probably not. I wouldn’t have been able to afford it. I dunno, maybe I probably would’ve – I dunno, got some money from somewhere (yeah). I would’ve like had to take out a huge loan or something, but I would’ve been gutted if I didn’t come. (Yeah) And if I didn’t get on the Network 75 programme.

Yeah, so it’s a really good idea, do you think?

Yeah, a very good idea.

Did they give you a choice of company to go and work for, or did they just find …?

Erm, well they rung me up and they said they had a place and did I want to go for an interview? And I didn’t feel the interview went very well, because a lot of things they were talking to me about I was like oh I don’t really understand that, but I was just blabbering away and erm when I got there I really liked the place, and I liked well the sound of what they’d done and when they said that I had the job, I just took it, so I don’t know whether they had others lined up for me.

Ok, what do the company that you work for do?

Er, they – they’re based in a small office and they sort of go out and work for other companies. Er, they work on like control systems, programmes erm IT, that sort of thing (yeah). So it’s a – they do a lot of things really, so it’s like erm not – you’re never doing the same thing it’s all project work.

OK, are there any other women in the company?

Er, there’s one but she’s sort of the admin sort of side of things – she don’t…

Not like in engineering or anything?

No.

OK – did you find it was a bit of a shock to the people that you were working with then, when you went in being a woman or … ?

I dunno. When I first started work, it didn’t feel as if they were shocked that I was a woman at all. Erm, I didn’t get the impression that that’s how they felt. Erm, I don’t think I get treated any different in work, where I work, it’s just when we go out on site (yeah). We had one occasion where we went to [company] where we do a lot of our work and we’d been out for dinner and we come back to sign in, in the car, and my work mate had gone in, and signed us both in and he said oh you can’t – women ain’t allowed on site. He didn’t realise I was one of the engineers, he thought he was just taking his wife or something in (yeah). He said, oh she can’t go in, and he had to explain to him then. So it’s just the way people see me doing it.

Yeah OK. What do you think are the best and the worst things about the working side of things?

Erm, the best is the money and the experience. Erm, it sort of makes learning here easier as well. You seem to click onto things, but I’d say the worst is having to work and coming here and doing your work as well. All those assignments after you’ve got home from work, and you never have a day off because all the days you have off from here you’re in work (yeah). But sometimes I’m lucky cos sometimes they let me sit in the office and catch up on a few assignments.

Oh that’s good – yeah.

If I haven’t got lots of work to do but that’s definitely the worst.

Yeah, OK, are there any other students at the company that you’re working for?

Er, there was one other when I started – that makes starting a bit easier because he came from the same college as me. But he left – I think it was just before Christmas but he left and done a totally different course (right) – he didn’t like the course. But I’m the only student there now.

OK – how do you think being at work differs from being at University? Do you think you get treated differently and what’s expected of you is different?

Erm, I don’t think I get treated differently, I think I put it on or – oh, I can’t do this assignment because I haven’t got enough time sort of thing, but they’re like a deadline’s a deadline and that’s it. If you work, you work. So, I wouldn’t say I get treated differently at all, for being in work.

OK, do you think that the course and being at work go together …?

Erm…

Or do you think they’re like two totally separate things?

Erm, they’re two totally separate things ‘cos they don’t work together. Work only knows what I do because I go back and tell them (yeah) and they sort of work around that but Network 75 don’t work with the course to plan things I should be doing at work. I’ve sort of done all that myself. I take in my books and I say these are the subjects I’m learning and they sort of work on that then.

Yeah, do you think that the Network 75 should do more on that side of things then or is it alright as it is?

Erm, they could do but mm, I don’t know how it’d be for other people but I’m alright at the moment because – I – it’s easy for me, just to go into work and say oh look, this is what I’m doing and they’ll sort of work it round me then but I wouldn’t say that they have to do that – no.

Ok, what do you think that you’ll be doing in say 5 years time then?

5 years time – well, my course is another 4 years (is it?) – yeah. Erm…

Do you think that you will go into the engineering industry?

Yeah – I’d like to work for my company I’m with now (yeah) just cos they’ve put me up since I’ve been in Uni, so I’d definitely work for them at the end of it. Erm, I dunno I haven’t really thought about what I’d do after the company.

What do you think could be your ideal career?

Erm, I wouldn’t mind running my own sort of company like I’m working for – so I’d be in charge then. Erm, so I can boss all the men around. But I wouldn’t change what I’m doing now – no.

OK, do you think that the career prospects are good in sort of your field of engineering?

Erm, no. Erm, it don’t seem to be that many places around that we could all work in because everywhere seems to be closing.

Yeah – does that worry you at all or…?

It does, but I’m hoping from being at Uni and getting the qualifications, I’ll always have a job out there for me (yeah). Maybe not doing exactly what I’m doing now but maybe sort of the same – similar thing.

OK – are you happy with all the career choices that you’ve made so far? If you went through everything again, from like leaving school, would you do anything differently?

Er, I don’t know because from doing all the different courses I’ve done at college and dropping out and working, erm like if I hadn’t have done that I don’t know whether I would’ve come to this course at the end of it (yeah). If I’d stayed doing my ‘A’ levels and – I’d probably be stuck at home now thinking what to do.

Doing something totally different?

Yeah, but if I went back I’d probably do exactly the same thing I’ve done now.

OK. How would you describe the engineering industry, from your experience?

Erm, well when – how would I describe it? A lot different to what you think it’s gonna be like (yeah).

What did you think it was going to be like?

I don’t know. From working in a factory you think it’s going to be like mass work and not – I knew it was going to be hard work, but lots of work. Being an engineer you sort of – you’re able to go on your pace and you can say what you want to do and – it’s a lot of freedom doing it as well, like it’s mad how many cups of coffee you get to drink, when you’re out on site and erm I got to be honest it’s not as hard work as I thought it was going to be. Like the sort of jobs I’ve been in, where you’re on the production line and you’re working and you’re working and you’re working, then you have a set break – it’s different to that. I find you’re left to – to do what you want to do really.

Yes, so it’s more relaxed.

Yeah, and you have more respect as well (yeah) being an engineer. Well I know I’m not one yet but sort of that atmosphere.

OK, would you describe the industry as male or masculine?

Mmm, working there now and being at Uni, I don’t see it as any different (yeah). I find people’s reactions, when I say what I’m doing – oh what are you doing at Uni? I’m doing electronics. And where do you work? Oh, I work for this company. Oh right. But to me I don’t see it as being any different. I don’t see why it should be erm male type of work. But I think that’s because I – I’ve done 3 years now studying, and I’ve done one year at work but when you first get in there you – I felt a bit awkward, but that goes within the first couple of weeks. But I wouldn’t – I wouldn’t say you get fussed over or anything like that because you’re a woman, ‘cos maybe for the first couple of days then, because I think that male have got to get used to it really (yeah) but now I don’t – I don’t see me as being any different.

OK, I think that’s everything then.

Erm, I – mm, well when I first started – even in college as well, you find they won’t speak to you – the boys – they, they go off in their own little gang, but then give it a couple of months and they come round and it just – it don’t feel no different now. Erm, I don’t know about encouraged but make it a bit easier – make it not seem so erm you can’t do it because you’re a woman (yeah). If they want to do it, they should – it should be made easier. Yeah, to get into. OK, what do you think makes a good engineer? Mm, I dunno. These are hard questions, isn’t it? Erm, (pause) erm, I can’t – I dunno. That’s OK. Do you think that there are any particular advantages or disadvantages to being a woman in engineering, or a woman in a male dominated environment? Erm, a lot of – well, being at Uni, they all reckon that I’m just gonna pass just ‘cos I’m a girl (right). Erm, but I wouldn’t say there’s many advantages in work – maybe, maybe people think that I’d get a job more easier because I’m a woman (yeah) but it don’t feel that way in work, it just feels equal, it don’t feel that I’m given anything to do because I’m a woman (yeah) and like when I say I don’t want to do something I still gotta do it. If I say I don’t want to get my hands dirty, they say you’ve still gotta do it, yeah. OK, has the course been what you expected it to be? Erm, in college it was – yeah, and then coming to Uni is a bit of a – a jump up. I found it a bit harder than I thought it was going to be here. Erm, but a lot of the stuff was what I thought it was going to be. It’s – I’d say it was a lot harder but I’m learning the stuff I wanted to learn. When you went to college, did you know that you wanted to come to Uni afterwards, or did you decide that when you got to the end of it? Mm, no I thought I could leave college and just go into work, but then during college I thought ah, I want to get an even better job so I come to Uni then. Ok then, what have been the best and the worst things about the course so far? Erm, oh, well the worst thing so far has been the exams at the end of the year. Erm, and having to get to know everyone else when we’ve come up here, ‘cos I think it was only last 2 weeks that I actually spoke to the rest of ‘em., during exam time, I’d never spoke to ‘em all the way through the year, really. (Yeah) Erm, erm, the best bits – I dunno – I can’t say oh I love it here, I love learning and – but I just enjoy – what it is I can’t say I love coming to Uni and doing all that work but I found the exams at the end of year the hardest because in college you erm – do little exams, everytime we’ve done a subject you sort of do little modules, whereas here you have to learn it all and do exams at the end. Erm, they’re coursework as well, I think they’re like split 70/30 and 50/50 but they were 3 hour exams – I don’t think I’ve ever sat an exam that long before. I hate exams (laughs) So it just – it just finished last week, now. So I’m working full time at the moment. Do you usually do that through all the holidays, do you work full time for the company? Yeah. OK, have you been taught by any female lecturers at all? Erm, there was one in college. Erm, first of all she started off just being a Maths teacher and then she taught some electronic subjects as well, but have I got any up here? No, I haven’t been taught by any up here – no. Really? Would you find it encouraging, do you think, to have more female lecturers? Erm, I don’t really think you would. As long as the teachers are good… Yeah. That’s OK. Do you think that the lecturers treat you the same as the male students? Mm, I don’t think they do to start with, I feel – I don’t say they treat me different it’s just little – little ways they speak to me or they talk to the whole class, boys, oh and girl, that sort of thing but come the first couple of weeks say, after that I’m just treated the same then. I think it’s just initially, at the beginning. It’s the same in work, when you meet different engineers they all won’t swear round me, and they all act differently, but that only lasts for the first couple of weeks and then they’re all the same then. Yeah. Just like the shock of seeing a woman? OK, do you have to do much group work as part of this Uni course? Erm, what you mean as part of the course year? Yeah. Erm, what happens is on a Wednesday, I think the people who come here work in groups to do little projects, but I miss out that lesson because I do that sort of thing in work. (yeah) And, instead of completing the lesson, I have to fill in a log book (right) of the stuff I do at work. So I – mm, if we do any practicals we get in groups of 2 or 3 (yeah) that’d only be for the one lesson. OK, do you use the skills that you’ve learnt at Uni in work, do you think? Erm, I’m just starting to now. When I first went there, erm not really – nothing I learnt in college – I couldn’t say really I used in work, but now I’m starting to pick up things and erm when we go on site, I seem to understand it a bit more now. I wouldn’t say I use anything I know, at the moment, but I seem to understand things more because of what I’ve learnt here. Yeah. Do you think it works the other way round as well? Do you think what you learn at work helps you understand things better at University? Yeah, definitely the other way round (yeah). It’s like erm, when you’re sat in the class and you learn all this and I thought do I really – have I really got to know all this? (yeah) Erm, and then when you go out to work then, you see why you have to know it. Maybe you don’t have to know it word for word in your head, because you’ll be able to look at books and instructions, but you see what it’s all used for then, when you go out to work. Yeah, OK. Why did you want to do the Network 75 programme? What appealed to you about doing that? Hmm, the money (yeah). And I’m glad I done it now. Yeah, OK. Do you think that you would have come to Uni then if you hadn’t had the Network 75 thing? Erm, probably not. I wouldn’t have been able to afford it. I dunno, maybe I probably would’ve – I dunno, got some money from somewhere (yeah). I would’ve like had to take out a huge loan or something, but I would’ve been gutted if I didn’t come. (Yeah) And if I didn’t get on the Network 75 programme. Yeah, so it’s a really good idea, do you think? Yeah, a very good idea. And I didn’t feel the interview went very well, because a lot of things they were talking to me about I was like oh I don’t really understand that, but I was just blabbering away and erm when I got there I really liked the place, and I liked well the sound of what they’d done and when they said that I had the job, I just took it, so I don’t know whether they had others lined up for me.
